commenter: Thomas A. Ciccone, Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Broadwind, Inc.

quotes.quote: Broadwind respectfully urges the Commission to adopt the Proposed Filer Rules substantially as proposed and, while the rulemaking remains pending, to provide an optional one-time transition accommodation

similarly situated registrants are already incurring significant costs to responsibly prepare for shortened filing deadlines, auditor attestation requirements, staffing additions, external advisor costs, and related compliance obligations that may apply for only a single reporting cycle

providing an optional, one-time transition period—such as a 12-month implementation grace period—during which affected registrants could defer the application of a newly triggered accelerated filer or large accelerated filer status
Broadwind further respectfully urges the Commission to consider making any such relief available as soon as possible, before adoption or effectiveness of final rules.

notes: Issuer (SRC, non-accelerated filer, float $75m-$700m, revenue >$100m) expecting to become an accelerated filer for FY2026. Attestation addressed only as a cost of the accelerated-filer transition it wants deferred; supports the proposal substantially as proposed, so position=support. Interim relief = one of the two issuers. Proposes that companies electing the transition accommodation disclose that election (p.3); coded asks_disclosure=false because it is disclosure of the election, not of whether an attestation was obtained -- flag for reconciliation. Revenue mentioned only as a fact about Broadwind, no revenue test proposed. Page 4 is blank.

commenter: Marc I. Steinberg, Radforf Chair and Professor of Law

quotes.quote: I write this comment letter in my individual capacity.
It rescinds the application of key provisions of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act for the vast majority of Exchange Act reporting companies (I understand roughly 80% of Exchange Act reporting companies).

notes: SMU law professor (letter dated May 27, 2026; docket date June 1). Constituency coded individual because he states he writes in his individual capacity (codebook: individual = person writing in a personal capacity); academic is the alternative a second coder may choose -- flag. Coded silent on attestation: the letter never mentions Section 404(b), auditor attestation or ICFR; its 'key provisions of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act' examples are say-on-pay and pay-versus-performance (actually Dodd-Frank). Borderline: the '80% of companies' SOX rescission could be read as an oblique reference to the 404(b) exemption; if so read, position would be do_not_expand. Commenter name kept as listed ('Radforf' is a typo for Radford).

commenter: Jen Sisson, CEO, International Corporate Governance Network (ICGN)

quotes.quote: We strongly oppose the changes which result in the removal of the auditor attestation requirement under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes Oxley Act (SOX) for companies other than large accelerated filers.
We therefore urge the Commission to retain the auditor attestation requirement for all reporting companies that are currently subject to Section 404(b).

Raising the Large Accelerated Filer threshold from US$700 million to US$2 billion would place most public companies into a much more fragmented disclosure regime and significantly reduce the information that must be made available to investors.
We do not support the proposed 60-month seasoning period before Large Accelerated Filer status can apply and instead recommend retaining the current 12-month period.

notes: Filed under S7-2026-17 (file prefix s7202617) but the letter expressly addresses both S7-2026-17 and S7-2026-18 and has a dedicated S7-2026-18 section (pp.3-10); coded normally, not_a_comment=false. Check docket index for any separate ICGN letter filed to S7-2026-18 (same_filer_as left null; not checked against other files). Investor association (members' AUM >US$100tn). Opposes any widening: wants 404(b) retained for all companies currently subject to it, and keep $700m, hence do_not_expand / oppose_any_increase. On-ramp: rejects 60 months, wants current 12 months. Notes FPI vs domestic inconsistency (p.6) but argues domestic companies should keep attestation, not for FPI parity relief: fpi_parity=false. Cites GAO-13-582 on disclosure in a footnote but makes no disclosure ask. 'If the Commission proceeds... appropriate transition arrangements should apply' plus monitoring/reinstatement process (p.7) is not interim relief for threshold-crossers. No alternative threshold proposed (retaining status quo is not an alternative).
